reason: Attacked hard, because this is the medium-confidence one, and it held. Translation drift is the live risk and the comparison page settles it: it sets three English Courages side by side and assigns this opening, word for word and with these lower case line heads, to Stanley Kunitz and Max Hayward, against two versions that read nothing like it. D. M. Thomas has We know what trembles in the scales, / What has to be accomplished. / The hour for courage. If all else fails, / With courage we are not unfurnished; Yevgeny Bonver has We know what is now on History's scales, / What is, in the world, going now. / The hour of courage shew our clock's hands. So the shipped wording is not a blend of the three and is not either rival. A second, independent search return carried the same quatrain and the continuation, Let bullets kill us, we are not afraid, nor are we bitter, though our housetops fall, and We will preserve you, Russian speech, under the Kunitz and Hayward credit. Attribution: the Russian poem is certainly Akhmatova's Muzhestvo, dated 23 February 1942, and the Russian original was read beside the English (Мы знаем, что ныне лежит на весах ... И мужество нас не покинет), so the four lines do render the opening quatrain and the locator lines 1 to 4 is right. Book and translator credit are as the title page gives them, Poems of Akhmatova, selected and translated by Stanley Kunitz with Max Hayward, Atlantic Monthly Press and Little, Brown, 1973. The lower case and and may at line heads are Kunitz's own sentence casing, confirmed in the reproduction, so the poem's own capitals rule is met. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Anna Akhmatova 0 of 3 for the year, not banned. In scope: poetry, published 1942, not scripture, lyric, proverb or oratory, and the quoted quatrain carries no wound or atrocity, so it is publishable; the graphic material in the poem is in the second quatrain, which is not quoted. Source line leads with the name, no dash, no straight double quote, 103 characters. Tag Poetry is the form. On theme it is the month's centre. ONE HONEST LIMIT TO CARRY IN THE NOTE, not a refutation: the printed 1973 page was still not opened, so the wording rests on reproductions that name the translators rather than on the book itself. I could not reach a scan; the Internet Archive copy is catalogued but the text is not open. The note should say plainly that the Kunitz and Hayward wording is attested in reproductions crediting that translation and the printed page was not seen.
